sources.title: Three-forms, Supersymmetry and String Compactifications

evidence.text: For Polonyi theory, promote b to a chiral multiplier X and introduce a complex-linear multiplet Σ. Eliminating Σ recovers constant X = b; eliminating X and Φ gives the special chiral field S = −D̄²Σ̄/4 and automatically produces the required boundary action.

sources.title: How many fluxes fit in an EFT?

evidence.text: Parent-action dualization promotes flux constants to real fields y_A and adds −dy_A∧A_3^A. Integrating out A_3 restores constant fluxes; integrating out y gives four-form field strengths and the dual action, including boundary terms.

sources.title: Exploring the Landscape of effective field theories

evidence.text: The local construction uses a chiral super-Weyl compensator, homogeneous kinetic and superpotential functions, and Einstein-frame gauge fixing. Chiral/linear multiplet duality is expressed through Legendre transforms.

sources.title: Three-forms in Supergravity and Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Promote superpotential coefficients to chiral superfields X_A and introduce real or complex-linear Lagrange-multiplier superfields. For constant G_AB, the multiplier equations make X_A constant (real r_A or complex c_A). For field-dependent G_AB with invertible M_AB=Im G_AB, they instead constrain M^{AB} Im X_B and yield X_A=e_A+G_AB(Φ)m^B, with constant real e_A,m^B; X_A generally remains field-dependent. Integrating out different fields yields either the original theory or constrained single/double three-form multiplets, including boundary terms.
